Definition: to cut off; specifically to shear a flock or shave the hair; figuratively to destroy an enemy
BiblicalUsage: Gazaz means to shear, to cut off the wool of a flock. Laban went to shear his sheep in Genesis 31:19, and Rachel stole his images while he was away. Nabal's shearers ate and drank at the feast in 1 Samuel 25:11, and Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor in 2 Samuel 13:23. The law forbids shearing the firstling of the sheep in Deuteronomy 15:19.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe shearing is the season when a man's heart shows. Laban sheared and lost his gods, Nabal feasted and refused a kindness, and Absalom's shearing feast ended in murder. I hold that the harvest feast tests what we truly love.
